taskVersion.name: ves-heldout-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station H-03, survey area H. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 193.6 | 0.90 | 0.90
2 | 129.1 | 3.18 | 4.08
3 | 29.1 | 0.79 | 4.87
4 | 29.8 | 26.64 | 31.51
5 | 165.4 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation for the given vertical electrical sounding (VES) data, we examine the resistivities of consecutive layers in groups of three.

The resistivity values for the five layers are:
- Layer 1: 193.6 $\Omega\text{-m}$
- Layer 2: 129.1 $\Omega\text{-m}$
- Layer 3: 29.1 $\Omega\text{-m}$
- Layer 4: 29.8 $\Omega\text{-m}$
- Layer 5: 165.4 $\Omega\text{-m}$

We evaluate each group of three consecutive layers:

1.  **Layers 1-2-3:**
    Resistivities: 193.6, 129.1, 29.1
    Comparison: $193.6 > 129.1 > 29.1$ (i.e., $\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3$)
    Pattern: **Q**

2.  **Layers 2-3-4:**
    Resistivities: 129.1, 29.1, 29.8
    Comparison: $129.1 > 29.1 < 29.8$ (i.e., $\rho_1 > \rho_2 < \rho_3$)
    Pattern: **H**

3.  **Layers 3-4-5:**
    Resistivities: 29.1, 29.8, 165.4
    Comparison: $29.1 < 29.8 < 165.4$ (i.e., $\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3$)
    Pattern: **A**

Combining these letters in depth order, we get the curve type QHA.

{"curve_type": "QHA"}
